headline: High-risk shared filesystem and shell overlap create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error exposure between ECC and ms-swift.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC reads/writes shared files and uses MCP, while ms-swift reads/writes files and consumes stdin/stdout plus APIs. If ms-swift outputs are copied into ECC-managed files or MCP inputs, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is written into an ECC-managed file or MCP payload
IF ECC parses file content as trusted instructions or skills
mitigations: Separate the two agents into different working directories
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted ms-swift outputs
Require a human review step before copying outputs into ECC files
Use read-only mounts for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches security findings, git history, and session data, and ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files. Both have filesystem access and network egress, so a shared workspace can move sensitive material from ECC into ms-swift outputs or uploads. This is a default-pathway risk if they share storage, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF ECC and ms-swift share a writable workspace
IF sensitive ECC artifacts are present in that workspace
IF ms-swift uploads or logs copied artifacts to external services
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and home directories
Exclude secrets and session files from shared mounts
Turn off uploads for any copied artifacts
Review logs for accidental secret capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, install packages, read and write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. ECC also modifies git state, while ms-swift does not, so the main conflict is concurrent writes to shared files and package state. Because ECC explicitly supports multiple instances and shared-state separation is mentioned, the risk is real but partially mitigable.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory or environment
IF either agent writes package state or git-tracked files concurrently
mitigations: Run each agent in its own directory
Serialize package installs and git operations
Use separate virtual environments
Avoid concurrent edits to shared config files
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces session summaries, learned skills, and security findings, and ms-swift consumes datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data. If ECC output is fed into ms-swift workflows without verification, ms-swift may act on incorrect or hallucinated instructions or metadata. The pathway is plausible in default CLI/file workflows, but not directly documented for this pair.
conditions: IF ECC outputs are used as ms-swift inputs without validation
IF ms-swift automation consumes those inputs as authoritative
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on transferred artifacts
Keep ECC outputs advisory, not authoritative
Log and diff transferred files before execution
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles security findings and session data, while ms-swift handles datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data. The profiles do not state residency, certification, or retention mismatches, so only a limited compliance concern is supported. I cite both because the risk arises from their combined handling of regulated-like artifacts, but the exact mismatch is not documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared logs or checkpoints
IF retention or residency policies differ across the two environments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared artifacts
Set short retention on logs and session files
Review export destinations before running either agent
Separate compliance-sensitive workloads
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy
